title: Yellowed Crusty Irish Bread Flatbread
description: A funky and festive Irish dish featuring strong white bread flour, perfect for a flexitarian-friendly meal or snack. This dehydrated flatbread is light and crusty, with a unique yellowed color.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, salt, sugar, and yeast.
Gradually add the warm water to the dry ingredients and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 10 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
Punch down the dough and shape it into a flat round.
Place the flatbread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, brush with olive oil, and bake for 20 minutes.
Remove the flatbread from the oven and let it cool on a wire rack.
Once the flatbread is cool, place it in a low temperature oven (150 degrees Fahrenheit) for 2 hours to dehydrate.
Remove the flatbread from the oven and let it cool completely before serving.
